Author: Krishan Pahal

HIGH COURT OF JUDICATURE AT ALLAHABAD ?Court No. - 79 Case :- CRIMINAL MISC ANTICIPATORY BAIL APPLICATION U/S 438 CR.P.C. No. - 3111 of 2023 Applicant :- Shiraz Siddiqui And Another Opposite Party :- State of U.P.

entities.text: HIGH COURT OF JUDICATURE AT ALLAHABAD
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
Counsel for Applicant :- Shahnawaz Khan,Ayyaz Khan Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Krishan Pahal,J.
List has been revised.
Heard Sri Ayyaz Khan, learned counsel for the applicants, Sri Yogesh Mishra, learned Additional Government Advocate for the State and perused the records.

The present anticipatory bail application has been filed on behalf of the applicants in Case Crime No.234 of 2022, under Sections 498A, 323, 354, 376, 504 and 506 IPC, 3/4 Dowry Prohibition Act and 3/4 Muslim Women (Protection of Rights on Marriage) Act, Police Station- Mahila Thana,
District Saharanpur with a prayer to enlarge them on anticipatory bail.

entities.text: Muslim Women (Protection of Rights on Marriage) Act
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: As per prosecution story, the marriage of the brother of the applicants was solemnized with the informant as per Muslim Rights on 26.10.2020.

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the applicants has stated that false allegations of rape have been levelled against the applicants, who happens to be the brother-in-law of the informant.

Learned counsel has further stated that the prosecution story stands falsified on the ground that as per the allegations in the FIR,
she has stated the date of occurrence to be 26.08.2022 while in her statement recorded u/s 164 Cr.P.C., she has stated the date of said occurrence to be 06.08.2022.
Learned counsel has further stated that the said contradiction is fatal to the prosecution story.
The applicants have been falsely implicated in the present case owing to their relation with the main accused person Almas Siddiqui.
Learned counsel has further stated that the applicants live separately to the husband of the informant and have nothing to do with the said offence.
Several other submissions have been made on behalf of the applicants to demonstrate the falsity of the allegations made against them.
The circumstances which, as per counsel, led to the false implication of the applicants have also been touched upon at length.
Learned counsel has further stated that the investigation is going on and the charge-sheet has not yet been filed.
There are no criminal antecedents of the applicants.

Learned counsel for the applicants has also stated that the applicants have co-operated in the investigation and undertakes that they will cooperate in the investigation in future also failing which the State can move appropriate application for cancellation of the anticipatory bail.
Per contra, learned AGA has vehemently opposed the anticipatory bail application but could not dispute the fact that there is no criminal history of the applicants.
Considering the overall facts and circumstances of the case, this Court is of the opinion that the applicants deserve to be granted anticipatory bail in connection with the aforesaid case.
, the Public Prosecutor/ Investigating Officer/ first informant-complainant is at liberty to file appropriate application for cancellation of anticipatory bail granted to the applicants.
